title: Charge endpoint deduplicated by idempotency key
source: Authored for the CodeReview benchmark corpus (expanded clean stratum), 2026-11-05
false_flag_note: A reviewer may flag the in-flight set as over-engineering or worry the gateway is called outside the lock. Holding the lock across the network call would serialise all payments; instead the key is claimed atomically under the lock (begin), the charge happens outside it, and the receipt is published under the lock (complete). A duplicate that arrives mid-charge gets DuplicateRequestInFlight instead of a second charge, a failed charge abandons the claim so a later retry can proceed, and the key is also passed to the gateway so retries are deduplicated downstream as well.

label_amendments.finding_title: None sentinel conflates with a falsy stored receipt, enabling a second charge

adjudication.probe_detail: gateway.charge returning None: two charge_once calls with same key caused 2 gateway charges (r1=None, r2=None); diff code executed verbatim. Stored None receipt is indistinguishable from the begin() no-prior sentinel.
